title: Known Science and Physical Principles: Autonomous Space Settlement Builders — Public Edition
description: Engineering record for Autonomous Space Settlement Builders (Interplanetary and Interstellar Civilization). Sets out the established scientific foundation: what is known, what the governing principles are, and where settled science ends and open questions begin.
body:
This record sets out the established scientific foundation: what is known, what the governing principles are, and where settled science ends and open questions begin. It covers Autonomous Space Settlement Builders — Robotic systems that survey sites, assemble habitats, and prepare infrastructure before human arrival.

Interplanetary civilization is a systems-integration challenge: propulsion gets you there, but ISRU, manufacturing, agriculture, medicine, and governance keep you there. Robotic precursors are the demonstrated path; crewed settlement is the debated one. Interstellar work is honest speculation bounded by physics: robotic probes at fractions of light speed are theoretically plausible; settlement architectures are research programs; generation ships and beyond are unresolved. Records here separate the expeditionary (near-term) from the civilizational (long-term).

Feasibility tier: THEORETICALLY-PLAUSIBLE. No known physical law forbids it, and paper studies or small-scale experiments suggest paths forward, but major engineering barriers stand between concept and reality. Records at this tier are explicit about which barriers are engineering and which would need new science.

The established science behind Autonomous Space Settlement Builders rests on Rocket equation plus life support plus economics: settlements must close their mass, energy, and value loops locally or be permanently subsidized from Earth. At the theoretically-plausible feasibility tier, the honest statement is this: the governing principles are understood on paper and in small experiments, with major open questions about whether they can be engineered into the described capability.

This is the public-edition record: it documents the publicly known research status of Autonomous Space Settlement Builders as engineering reference. It claims nothing beyond the evidence, and every speculative element carries its feasibility tier openly — never presented as established fact.
